title: jmap-mail-types' Keyword(String) newtype lacks #[non_exhaustive]; 8 sibling workspace newtypes carry it — canonical extension-types template has the laxest single-field-newtype derive shape
description:
**Divergence** — opaque-string newtype family across jmap-types + jmap-mail-types + jmap-jscalendar-types:

| Crate | Newtype | `#[non_exhaustive]`? |
|---|---|---|
| jmap-types | `Id(String)` | yes |
| jmap-types | `UTCDate(String)` | yes |
| jmap-types | `Date(String)` | yes |
| jmap-types | `State(String)` | yes |
| jmap-jscalendar-types | `LocalDateTime` | yes |
| jmap-jscalendar-types | `Duration` | yes |
| jmap-jscalendar-types | `SignedDuration` | yes |
| jmap-jscalendar-types | `UTCOffset` | yes |
| jmap-mail-types | `Keyword(String)` (src/keyword.rs:89-91) | **NO** |

jmap-mail-types describes itself as the canonical extension-types template, yet has the laxest single-field-newtype derive shape in the workspace.

**Caller-observable / maintainer cost**: a future maintainer who wants to add a derived-internal field (cached lowercase form, validation flag, etc.) to `Keyword` cannot do so without a SemVer-major. The same change to `Id` / `LocalDateTime` would be non-breaking.

**Fix**: one-line attribute addition to crate-jmap-mail-types/src/keyword.rs:89-91. cargo test --workspace passes unchanged (no caller relies on outside-crate struct-literal construction of `Keyword`).
